entries.clue: Arranged brief sale for stand out art piece (3,6)

indicators.note: arranged letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone sets up a quick sale to sell off a striking work of art.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stand out' reads as praise for the art, but it is literal: this kind of carving has figures standing out slightly from a flat background.
annotation.definitionFit: A bas relief is a sculpture with shallow raised figures, a piece of art that literally stands out.

entries.clue: Forbid alcohol store reportedly providing dessert (7)

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the sound stands in for the spelling

blocks.note: to ban = to forbid
an offie is British slang for an off-licence, a shop selling alcohol

annotation.surface: A ban on the drinks shop somehow leads to pudding.
annotation.walkthrough: An off-licence is a British shop licensed to sell alcohol to take away, nicknamed the offie; the pie is spelt both banoffee and banoffi.
annotation.definitionFit: Banoffi is a British dessert of banana, toffee and cream on a biscuit base.

entries.clue: Extremely shy neurotic he’d got working in harmony (7)

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of SHY
first and last letters of NEUROTIC, still under 'Extremely'
HE'D with the apostrophe dropped

annotation.surface: A timid, anxious man somehow manages to fit in with everyone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' serves both the next two words, so shy and neurotic each give up only their ends; 'he'd' is taken as it stands.
annotation.definitionFit: To have synched is to have got things working in time together, in harmony.

entries.clue: Happy to acquire a short cane that’s expandable (11)

indicators.note: what is acquired is taken inside
a short word is missing its last letter

blocks.note: elated = very happy; it opens after its first two letters
A + STICK without its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone is pleased to buy a small walking cane that can be extended.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short' trims only the cane, not the A before it, and the happy word does the acquiring, so it goes on the outside.
annotation.definitionFit: Elasticated fabric has elastic sewn in, so it can stretch and expand.

entries.clue: Reverse cuts in listings (7)

indicators.note: reverse the order of the two parts, so the second comes first

blocks.note: used as it stands
dices = cuts into cubes

annotation.surface: An instruction to undo the cuts made to some published lists.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' here swaps the order of the two pieces as the clue gives them, rather than turning any letters back to front.
annotation.definitionFit: Indices, the plural of index, are alphabetical listings at the back of a book.

entries.clue: Type of of hose used on trawlers? (7)

definitions.text: Type of of hose used on trawlers?

blocks.note: read as a kind of hosepipe, and meant as hose in its old sense of stockings; the doubled 'of' is a typo in the printed clue
trawlers are fishing boats that drag mesh through the sea, and the question mark says the link is a joke

annotation.surface: A question about the kind of hosepipe a fishing boat carries.
annotation.walkthrough: Fishnet stockings are made of an open mesh like a fishing net, so the clue pretends the stockings are what a trawler uses.
annotation.definitionFit: Fishnet is an open-mesh fabric used for stockings, named after the nets fishing boats haul.

entries.clue: Admit everyone has pained expression (5)

blocks.note: all = everyone
ow! is what you say when hurt

annotation.surface: Everyone grimaces when they have to confess something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pained expression' looks like a grimace, but it is a spoken expression: the cry of someone hurt.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of conceding: you allow or admit that an opponent has a point.

entries.clue: Atmosphere occasionally seen in aviary (3)

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used, every other one

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters

annotation.surface: The feel of a bird enclosure is noticed now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' asks for letters taken at intervals, here every other letter starting with the first.
annotation.definitionFit: Air is the atmosphere around us, and also the mood of a place.

entries.clue: Be open about place being spartan (3,4)

blocks.note: to lay = to place, as in lay the table
a spartan room is bare

annotation.surface: Being candid about a location that has no comforts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Place' looks like a noun for a location, but it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: stripping a thing so nothing covers it, used of feelings or secrets exposed candidly.

entries.clue: Expanded group dictates how observers may be separated (4,3)

blocks.note: expanded = broad, and a group = a collection
observers are eyes, which may sit far apart on a face

annotation.surface: A bigger group lays down rules on how onlookers should be spaced apart.
annotation.walkthrough: The observers are not people but eyes, and 'dictates' only joins the two definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Wide-set describes eyes spaced well apart, and a wide set is an expanded group.

entries.clue: Fighter captured by cameraman in Jaipur (5)

indicators.note: the answer is held inside the words that follow

blocks.note: cameramaN IN JAipur

annotation.surface: A fighter is caught on film by a cameraman in the Indian city of Jaipur.
annotation.walkthrough: Jaipur is a city in India, and the cameraman is there only for his last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A ninja is a Japanese fighter trained in stealthy martial arts.

entries.clue: Document about small ancient city in ruins … (9)

indicators.note: the outer word goes about, around, the rest

blocks.note: a deed is a legal document; it opens in the middle
S = small, as on clothing labels
Troy, the city of the Trojan War

annotation.surface: A record of a small ancient city lying in ruins.
annotation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue on into 11 across, but the two parse separately; Troy is also a city that famously lay in ruins.
annotation.definitionFit: Something destroyed is wrecked, left in ruins.

entries.clue: … note it is lacking in credence (3)

indicators.note: IT is missing from the word that follows

blocks.note: faith = credence, belief
the clue's own word, the two letters taken out of the middle

annotation.surface: Following on from 10 across: a remark that something is simply not believable.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale (doh, ray, me, fah); 'it' is the letters to remove, not a pronoun.
annotation.definitionFit: Fah is a musical note, the fourth of the tonic sol-fa scale.

entries.clue: He contracts redevelopment experts (11)

indicators.note: redevelopment rebuilds the letters into something new

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: A builder signs contracts for specialists to regenerate a site.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contracts' reads as a verb about hiring, but it is just letters to rearrange along with 'He'.
annotation.definitionFit: Technocrats are technical experts, especially ones given power to run things.

entries.clue: Local market where might Americans shop for trunks? (3,4,4)

definitions.text: Local market where might Americans shop for trunks?

blocks.note: a British market held in a field or car park, where people sell unwanted goods laid out from their cars
read as buying luggage or swimwear, and meant as Americans calling the back of a car its trunk

annotation.surface: A question about where Americans buy luggage or swimming trunks.
annotation.walkthrough: What the British call a car boot, Americans call a car trunk, so to an American the British market sounds like a place to buy trunks.
annotation.definitionFit: A car boot sale is a local market where goods are sold from the boots of parked cars.

entries.clue: Initiates popular channels (7)

blocks.note: in = fashionable, popular
ducts are channels for air or fluid

annotation.surface: Something starts off the favourite TV stations.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Initiates' looks like starts, but it means admits to a society, and 'channels' are pipes, not TV stations.
annotation.definitionFit: To induct someone is to initiate them formally into a post or society.

entries.clue: Wrong clothing for soldiers? It’s a real pain (7)

indicators.note: what clothes something wraps around it

blocks.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law; it opens before its last letter
men = soldiers, as in officers and men

annotation.surface: Being issued the wrong uniform is agony for the troops.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clothing' looks like a noun for uniforms, but it is the verb: the wrong wraps around the soldiers.
annotation.definitionFit: A torment is a source of great suffering, a real pain.

entries.clue: London perhaps almost put a limit on everything (7)

indicators.note: almost all of the phrase, so its last letter goes

blocks.note: cap it all = put a limit on everything

annotation.surface: A plea to restrict everything in London.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'put a limit on everything' as a three-word phrase, then shorten it by a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: London is a capital city; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.

entries.clue: In Westminster a backbencher rises partly for show (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising letters read from bottom to top
only part of the words is used

blocks.note: westminsTER A BACkbencher

annotation.surface: A backbench MP stands up in Parliament purely for show.
annotation.walkthrough: Westminster is the home of the British Parliament, and a backbencher is an MP without a government post; 'rises' fits the MP standing to speak.
annotation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a show of songs and sketches in a club or restaurant.

entries.clue: Settled up front to get help with homework (7)

blocks.note: prep is British school slang for homework
aid = help

annotation.surface: A parent pays in advance for a homework tutor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' only puts the help alongside the homework, and the homework comes first in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Prepaid means paid for in advance, settled up front.

entries.clue: Field quietly blooming – it will be obvious immediately (4,3)

blocks.note: a lea is a poetic word for a meadow
p = piano, quietly in music
flowers that are out are in bloom

annotation.surface: A meadow quietly bursts into flower and the change is plain to see at once.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks like an adjective for the field, but it is flowers being out.
annotation.definitionFit: Something that leaps out at you is obvious at first glance.

entries.clue: Selection of sweet treats with calories reduced by a third (7)

definitions.note: Selection is singular, the answer plural; a selection is a range of choices

indicators.note: the treats have three Cs, and one of them goes

blocks.note: choc ices are chocolate-coated ice-cream bars
C = calories, removed once

annotation.surface: A range of desserts made lighter by cutting a third of the calories.
annotation.walkthrough: The trick is that the treats hold three Cs, so losing one C is losing a third of the calories.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a selection offered to a customer is a range of options to pick from.

entries.clue: Thickly covered in rum and coke (5,2)

indicators.note: rum is an old British word for odd, so the letters come out strange

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: Someone is drenched in a rum and coke.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rum and coke' reads as a drink, but rum is the indicator, meaning odd, and 'and coke' is the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Make-up or mud caked on lies in a thick crusted layer.

entries.clue: Company distributed legal art compilation (7)

indicators.note: letters distributed are spread into a new order

blocks.note: Co. = company
LEGAL rearranged

annotation.surface: A firm hands out an anthology of legal artworks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Legal art' reads as a genre; 'legal' is the fodder and 'art' belongs to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A collage is an artwork made by assembling scraps of paper, photos and other materials.

entries.clue: Navy and Airforce assets accept conservative discipline (7)

indicators.note: what the words accept goes inside them

blocks.note: a submarine is a naval vessel
jets are air force planes; this one opens before its last letter
C = Conservative

annotation.surface: The armed forces take on a traditionalist approach to training.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Assets' serves both services: a vessel for the navy and a plane for the air force; the conservative goes inside the second.
annotation.definitionFit: A subject is an academic discipline, such as history or physics.

entries.clue: Money collection to establish a major source of food (11)

blocks.note: bread is slang for money
a basket is a collection, as in a basket of goods

annotation.surface: A fundraiser to set up a big food bank.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Money collection' reads as a charity whip-round, but it is two separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A breadbasket is a region that grows much of a country's grain, a major source of food.

entries.clue: Launch campaign – by dropping out! (3)

indicators.note: the named letters drop out of the word

blocks.note: to lobby = to campaign for a cause
the clue's own word, its two letters struck off the end

annotation.surface: A political campaign starts, but only by quitting the race.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like a preposition but is the letters to remove.
annotation.definitionFit: To lob is to launch something high through the air.

entries.clue: Call out revision of a dour deal (4,5)

indicators.note: a revision rewrites the letters in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone demands that a miserable agreement be renegotiated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Call out' suggests objecting to the deal, but it means say the words for all to hear.
annotation.definitionFit: To read something aloud is to call it out so others hear.

entries.clue: Lots wanting leader – it doesn’t matter which (3)

indicators.note: the word lacks its first letter

blocks.note: many = lots; its leader M goes

annotation.surface: A crowd without a head, where no one cares who takes charge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' means lacking, not desiring, so the lots lose their first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Any, as in 'take any', means whichever one, it does not matter which.

entries.clue: Saw madam digest stuff from the centre (5)

indicators.note: take the stuff at the centre of each word

blocks.note: the middle of M-ADA-M
the middle of DI-GE-ST

annotation.surface: A lady is seen eating the middle out of something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see; here it is the noun for an old saying.
annotation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb, which is what an adage is.

entries.clue: Currently, father is appearing in play (5)

indicators.note: the first piece appears inside the second

blocks.note: to toy = to play; it opens before its last letter
da = dad, father

annotation.surface: Right now, Dad has a part in a stage play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a theatre piece, but it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of nowadays: the world today is the world as it currently is.

entries.clue: Most kind to one winding up in trial (9)

indicators.note: ends up inside the next word

blocks.note: a test is a trial; it opens after its first letter
one who ends, winds things up, is an ender

annotation.surface: Leniency shown to a defendant who has landed in court.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Winding up' does double duty: the one is someone who winds things up, and the phrase also puts that person inside the trial.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: tender means kind and gentle, and this is its superlative.
